refuses_on: torn-expansion — an UNCLOSED `$(` or `${`. A substitution that RAN cannot leave one (unterminated is a shell syntax error and the command never executes), so the text is a fragment of a partially-quoted argument.
empty-parameter-expansion — a literal `${}`. Also a shell syntax error, so it cannot be a surviving literal from a working command line, and it is not prose either.
control-characters — C0/DEL other than tab and newline: ANSI escape residue from capturing a colourised tool's output. No information, and it corrupts every reader of the JSONL stream.
residue-only — after stripping whitespace and shell punctuation nothing is left: every word expanded away and only the skeleton remains.
warns_on: expansion-syntax-survived — `$(`, `${`, `$NAME`, `$0`/`$1`, `$?` or a backtick still present. These SURVIVED, so THIS call was quoted correctly; the warning is that the same text through DOUBLE quotes would have been silently rewritten.
collapsed-whitespace — an interior run of 2+ spaces. The ONE real-incident shape the tool can see: an eaten code span leaves nothing but the doubled space (steward seq-147 quotes exactly that).
unbalanced-backticks — an odd number of backticks, i.e. a torn code span.
tc53.boundary_rationale: The refusal set is the intersection of (a) 'cannot plausibly be what any author meant' and (b) zero occurrences across the whole real corpus. The corpus run DECIDED the boundary rather than confirming it: `$()` was drafted as a refusal and was demoted to a warning because TC-53's own summary contains that literal text as prose. `$0 probe`, `~$1.77` and single-quoted code spans are ordinary here and are warn-only for the same reason. Odd-backtick-count was drafted as a refusal (0 in the corpus) and demoted too, because a lone backtick discussing the character itself is plausible and TC-121 is the live precedent for what a false positive costs: seat-path-guard.sh read prose as a write target and two different agents independently routed around it. This tool sits on the active commit path (scripts/hooks/pre-commit via check-staged-ledger-sidecars.sh) and is named by three seat/command definitions, so a false refusal blocks the Steward mid-ruling and the next step is a hand-append to an append-only ledger — strictly worse than the corruption. Every refusal therefore names the single-quoting fix with a copy-pasteable form AND the one override, `--accept-shell-residue`, which writes the record and names the waived classes on stderr. HONESTY NOTE, stated in the docstring, the commit message and the README rather than papered over: the shell expands before ledgerwrite runs, so the guard sees RESIDUE and never INTENT, and NONE of the three measured incidents (seq-95/96, seq-108/109, the one quoted in seq-147) is detectable in-tool. That is why A2 (dev/steward/README.md) is half the fix and not garnish.

tc92.why: Two reasons, both about risk. (1) commission-manifest.sh's token derivation and design scan live inside a `python3 - <<'PY'` heredoc; extracting them into scripts/lib/ is a real refactor of the single most load-bearing generator in the commissioning path, and the design_refs mechanism's whole safety argument is the byte-identity of its output. Driving the tool instead means commission-manifest.sh is UNMODIFIED, so byte-identity is true by construction rather than by test. (2) The check consumes the manifest's OWN per-token coverage report (`NO design doc mentions: …`, and the `ZERO design docs matched … (tokens: …)` hard-failure), so the two literally cannot disagree about a slice's tokens. TC-100 is the standing proof that the matching rule is subtle. The ONE piece that had to be reproduced — the whole-token boundary, needed to test CURATED documents the manifest's walker never opens — is asserted byte-identical to the manifest's token_re() AT EVERY RUN (LOOKBEHIND/LOOKAHEAD literals), and DESIGN_ROOTS is parsed out of the manifest source rather than restated. If either changes, the check exits 2 instead of answering a different question from the report it consumes (arm 6b).
tc92.predicate: PER-TOKEN. Every token a ladder entry declares must be whole-token matched by a design document under the manifest's selectors (i), or by one of the entry's curated `design_refs` documents (ii), or carry a frozen exemption (iii).
tc92.predicate_deviation_from_brief: The brief stated route (ii) as 'the entry carries a non-empty design_refs' — a PER-ENTRY blanket pass. Implemented as PER-TOKEN instead ('a curated doc that NAMES the token'), because the per-entry reading is inconsistent with two other things the brief states as load-bearing. First, the brief's measured baseline names BOTH Slice 20/TC-45 and Slice 21/ac_002 as exemptions; under the per-entry reading Slice 21 already carries a non-empty design_refs, so it would be covered by (ii) and its exemption row would be dead code — an exemption that exempts nothing is a lie in the source. Second, the brief's stated ratchet property is 'a NEW uncovered token goes red immediately, on a landed slice or a future one'; under the per-entry reading a new id minted on any of slices 21, 22, 23, 31, 32 or 33 (all of which carry design_refs today) would never fire — the exact quiet mode TC-92 is about. The per-token rule is the only one under which the brief's own baseline and its own stated purpose are both true. Curation is still a real remedy and is proven so by arm 4: a curated document OUTSIDE the scanned roots that names the token DOES provide coverage, which is the case the manifest's walker can never reach. FLAGGING IT rather than absorbing it silently.

tc92.exemption_semantics: Frozen and individually enumerated inside scripts/check-design-refs.sh with a TC-92 pointer. Anything NOT in the table is a hard failure. Deliberately NOT 'skip LANDED slices' — the check never reads a ladder entry's `status` field at all, so it cannot branch on one (arm 11 asserts both the structural and the behavioural half). A STALE exemption (one whose token has since gained coverage) is reported loudly on stdout and is NEVER fatal, so paying coverage debt can never be the thing that turns the tree red.
tc92.wiring: scripts/hooks/pre-commit only — the ACTIVE hook (core.hooksPath = scripts/hooks), invoked as `scripts/check-design-refs.sh --staged-only`, placed immediately after the TC-88 sidecar block and mirroring its shape. The trigger set lives in ONE place, the gate's own --staged-only branch: `^dev/plans/release-state-.*\.json$|^dev/design/`, scanned with NO --diff-filter so DELETIONS trigger it too (codex P2-1). When it fires, the sweep runs over a snapshot of the INDEX built with `git checkout-index --all --prefix` into mktemp -d, with the git environment scrubbed, so it judges the content that will be committed rather than the worktree (codex P2-2). Measured: ~7ms exit 0 when nothing relevant is staged; 2.4s for the full 14-slice sweep when a dev/design path IS staged. Deliberately NOT added to scripts/preflight.sh --landing (every check there is paired with a mirrored CI job and this one has no mirror, and adding the mirror was forbidden), NOT to scripts/agent-test.sh, and nothing under .github/** was modified. Arm 9 pins the CI-inertness.

findings.title: Include staged design deletions in the trigger
findings.defect: `git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR` excludes deletions, so a commit that REMOVES the only dev/design/** document mentioning a token hit the early exit and the sweep never ran. Coverage could be deleted through the gate.
findings.fix: Dropped the --diff-filter entirely for the trigger scan (the same shape check-staged-ledger-sidecars.sh uses). A deleted path decides only WHETHER to run; the sweep now reads an index snapshot, so it never attempts to open a deleted file. Commented in place so the omission cannot be 'tidied' back in.
findings.test: arm 13 — stages `git rm dev/design/widget-design.md` (the sole design of record for Slice 0's two tokens) and requires the gate to both FIRE and FAIL. RED against the pre-fix gate with rc=0 and empty output.

findings.title: Validate the staged snapshot, not the worktree
findings.defect: The sweep drove commission-manifest.sh against the WORKING TREE while gating the INDEX. Under a partial commit that is wrong in both directions: a staged ladder entry minting an id passes because the back-link exists only as an UNSTAGED edit (silent false PASS — the quiet mode TC-92 exists to stop, arriving through the gate built to stop it), and an unrelated unstaged edit can REFUSE a clean staged commit (false BLOCK on the active commit path — the TC-121 hazard).
findings.route_taken: PREFERRED — exact by construction. `git checkout-index --all --prefix` materialises the index into a mktemp -d tree and the manifest is driven there.
findings.route_rationale: The brief made this purely empirical, so it was measured BEFORE anything was built. (1) commission-manifest.sh needs git for exactly one thing — `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` at line 125; every other `git log`/`git rev-parse` occurrence in the file is emitted PROSE, not an invocation. (2) An empty `git init -q --template=` inside the snapshot satisfies it, and the manifest's stdout for 0.8.20 Slice 22 run inside the snapshot is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the worktree run. (3) Cost: `git checkout-index --all` = 0.255s for 2121 files / 66M. With all three green there was no reason to take the bounded fallback, so it was not built. commission-manifest.sh is UNMODIFIED and byte-identity is re-verified 14/14. No `git stash` anywhere near the commit path.
findings.hazard_found_and_closed: Hooks leak git environment. MEASURED with a probe hook on this machine's git: GIT_DIR is unset but `GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index` IS exported, and it is RELATIVE — so a git invocation with cwd inside the snapshot would resolve against the real repository and silently undo the snapshot; some git versions export GIT_DIR too. GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR and GIT_PREFIX are all unset before the sweep runs. Arm 17 reproduces the hook environment and pins that the verdict is unchanged.

codex_review.residual_stated_honestly: Two states cannot be certified and are ANNOUNCED LOUDLY on stderr as NOT CHECKED and then let through (exit 0), never failed: an UNMERGED index (no stage 0 to snapshot) and a snapshot that cannot be built (checkout-index failure). This deliberately DIVERGES from check-staged-ledger-sidecars.sh, which exits 2 on an unmerged path — that gate protects an invariant conflict resolution actively breaks, whereas this one is a coverage discipline where a refusal nobody can act on costs more than the miss, and a merge commit touching dev/design/** must not be blocked by a gate that could not look. It is a considered divergence, not an oversight, and it is written into the script header (THE RESIDUAL, NAMED RATHER THAN IMPLIED) as well as here. No comment anywhere implies index-exactness the code does not have.

finding.title: Scrub the git env BEFORE `git init`, not after
finding.defect: `git init -q --template= "$SNAPSHOT"` ran while GIT_DIR was still exported. With GIT_DIR set, git init does NOT create $SNAPSHOT/.git — GIT_DIR wins and git REINITIALISES THE REPOSITORY GIT_DIR NAMES.
finding.codex_claim_corrected: codex predicted the gate would BLOCK the commits it certifies. MEASURED: it did not. The verdict stayed correct because commission-manifest.sh's `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` degrades to `cd ""`, a bash no-op returning 0, leaving it in the snapshot. The real consequences were (a) a WRITE INTO THE REAL REPOSITORY and (b) the mechanism silently resting on behaviour POSIX leaves unspecified. The P1 is entirely correct; only its predicted symptom differed, and the actual one is worse.

codex_review.route_taken: Option 1 — hand-build a minimal .git inside $SNAPSHOT with mkdir and printf; NO git binary invoked to create it, and NO `git init` anywhere in the script.
codex_review.route_rationale: Chosen over the option-2 fallback because it keeps codex P2-2 fully closed. Option 2 (compare index vs worktree, and report NOT CHECKED on divergence) creates no snapshot and is safe, but it degrades to 'cannot certify' in exactly the partial-commit case P2-2 is about, so the coverage gap would reopen whenever it matters most. Option 1 keeps the sweep index-exact AND makes the write-safety structural. Measured before adopting: a HEAD, a config with repositoryformatversion 0 and bare false, and empty objects/ and refs/heads/ is all `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` needs, resolving correctly from the snapshot root and from any subdirectory. Chosen over 'reorder the scrub' because ordering makes damage UNLIKELY while removing the write makes it IMPOSSIBLE, and a guard on the commit path must not be able to damage what it guards.
codex_review.why_write_safety_is_structural: The script invokes exactly five git commands and every one is read-only: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (twice — once to find the repo root, once scrubbed via `env -u` to prove the snapshot resolves to itself), `git --no-optional-locks diff --cached --name-only`, `git ls-files --unmerged`, and `git checkout-index --all --prefix=` which writes ONLY inside the mktemp -d snapshot. `--no-optional-locks` was added so that even the trigger scan cannot refresh the index stat cache, because a read-only claim with an exception is a claim nobody can rely on. There is no git init, no git config, no git add, no git stash. With no write anywhere in the path, the worst case of a leaked or wrong GIT_* is a WRONG ANSWER FROM A DOCS-HYGIENE GATE — never a damaged repository. Verified by a code-only audit (comments stripped) over the full write-verb list.
codex_review.belt_and_braces: After materialising the snapshot the gate requires `$SNAPSHOT/.git` to exist AND the snapshot's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (run through `env -u`, on the same invocation, so no later edit can separate them) to resolve to $SNAPSHOT itself. Anything else prints NOT CHECKED and exits 0. This removes the dependence on `cd ""` being a bash no-op — the accidental correctness that let the defect hide.
codex_review.scrub_retained: The `unset` of the seven GIT_* variables stays, as DEFENCE IN DEPTH rather than as the safety argument, and still sits AFTER the last real-repo read. That ordering is now a CORRECTNESS requirement rather than a safety one: `checkout-index` must see the hook's GIT_INDEX_FILE, because a partial commit (`git commit -- <paths>`) puts the content that will be committed into a TEMPORARY index and names it there (measured: `.git/next-index-*.lock`). Arm 17d pins it.
codex_review.arm_17_rebuild: The predecessor arm 17 PASSED WHILE THE DEFECT WAS LIVE, which is the more serious half of this round. It hand-made `GIT_DIR=.git GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index` — both RELATIVE — which is the shape a PLAIN checkout exports and is harmless. A real LINKED-WORKTREE hook exports both as ABSOLUTE, and it is the absolute GIT_DIR that breaks git init. The arm now builds a genuine worktree with `git worktree add`, installs a genuine hook, makes a genuine commit, and asserts NON-VACUITY FIRST: if the captured GIT_DIR is not absolute the arm FAILS rather than passing, because it would be testing the same fiction.

red_evidence.arm_17c: GREP-ONLY, no execution, safe against any revision. Comments stripped, then the full git write-verb list matched: `edcce999 CODE invokes: git init`; `HEAD invokes: (none)`.
red_evidence.arm_17b_and_17d: Captured BEFORE the freeze, against edcce999 in a throwaway fixture: arm 17b `signature changed=YES` (the gate rewrote the gated repository's .git/config); arm 17d `checkout-index=215 unset=231 init=225` — the scrub sat 6 lines too late, after git init.
red_evidence.arm_17_rebuilt: HONEST NON-RESULT: it PASSES against edcce999 too, because the verdict genuinely stayed correct via the `cd ""` degradation. codex asked for both arms RED; one of them cannot be, and contriving an assertion to force red would be the same vacuous-green disease in reverse. The write-safety arms carry the RED.

finding.title: `readlink -f` is GNU-only and the self-check FAILED OPEN
finding.defect: The snapshot self-check compared `readlink -f "$SNAP_TOP"` with `readlink -f "$SNAPSHOT"`. BSD/macOS readlink has no -f, so BOTH substitutions collapse to the empty string, `"" != ""` is false, and the guard whose entire job is to prove the toplevel resolved INSIDE the snapshot silently passes. It also sprayed readlink errors into hook output.
finding.class: A check that goes green because both of its inputs degraded identically — the same vacuous-green disease as the old arm 17. Third appearance of this class in this unit, which is why the fix was applied beyond the reported line.
finding.fix: Replaced with the repo's existing portable idiom, `abs_dir() { ( cd "$1" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P ); }`, lifted from scripts/preflight.sh whose comment already explains why not to use readlink -f. AND made to FAIL CLOSED: if either normalised path is empty that is NOT CHECKED + exit 0, so empty-equals-empty is not a reachable pass.
finding.proof: Reproduced in isolation with a BSD-behaving readlink stub and genuinely mismatched paths — old idiom: PASSES (fail-open); new idiom: REFUSES. Grep-only RED for arm 17g: `readlink -f` at line 320 of 071f4d38, nothing at HEAD.

codex_review.same_class_fixed_in_my_own_arms: Two round-2 arms — the ones added specifically to catch fail-open — were themselves fail-open on BSD. `admin_signature()` piped GNU `find -printf` into `md5sum`, and the primary-config canary piped `cat` into `md5sum`; with either tool absent both sides hash nothing and compare equal, so the arm passes regardless. Both now use POSIX `cksum` and both assert their raw input was NON-EMPTY before trusting the comparison. Not asked for, but it is the identical defect in the guards meant to catch it.

portability_audit.method: comments stripped from both files, then matched against readlink -f, grep -P, sed -i, stat -c, date -d, date +%s%N, md5sum, find -printf, realpath, mktemp flags, env -u
portability_audit.gate: CLEAN — no GNU-only construct remains. `env -u` is POSIX. `mktemp -d` matches existing repo usage. `git --no-optional-locks` is a git flag (2.15+), not a coreutils one.
portability_audit.test: Two GNU dependencies retained, deliberately, because neither can go green over a defect: `find -printf` in admin_listing now FAILS CLOSED via the new non-empty guard, and `date +%s%N` in the timing arm FAILS LOUD (on BSD `%N` stays literal and the arithmetic aborts). The suite is local-only and Linux-only by existing convention; one other repo suite already uses `find -printf`.
portability_audit.note: `readlink -f` appears in scripts/preflight.sh only inside the comment that tells you not to use it. Before this fix, scripts/check-design-refs.sh was the ONLY script in scripts/*.sh that actually invoked it.

finding.title: Failed normalisation cannot reach the self-check (set -e aborts the assignment)
finding.defect: Under `set -e`, `SNAP_TOP_ABS="$(abs_dir …)"` exits the script when abs_dir returns nonzero, so the documented `NOT CHECKED` + `exit 0` branch was UNREACHABLE in exactly the circumstance it was written for. The hook received a bare `exit 1` with no message — a silent false BLOCK on the commit path.
finding.verified_independently: A `set -e` assignment from a failing command substitution dies before the next statement runs (measured, isolated repro). And `|| true` restores reachability with an empty value.

fix.2: `|| true` on BOTH substitutions — `SNAPSHOT_ABS` was checked, not assumed, and has the identical exposure.
fix.3: abs_dir now rejects an empty argument: `[ -n "$1" ] || return 1`.
fix.untouched: The `-z` guards and the `!=` comparison are byte-for-byte unchanged, as instructed. No neighbouring line, no other arm, nothing else in either file.
fix.comment: The adjacent comment now records WHY there is no default, so it does not get reinstated.

codex_review.deviation_from_the_prescription_and_why: The brief authorised exactly two changes: drop the default, and stop the abort. Applied literally, those two alone introduce a FALSE PASS. MEASURED: `cd ""` SUCCEEDS in bash and `pwd -P` then returns THE CURRENT DIRECTORY — which at that point IS the snapshot — so an empty toplevel normalises to the very value it is compared against, the `-z` test never fires because the result is non-empty, the comparison matches, and the guard silently passes. The brief's own text anticipated the mechanism ('bash cd "" succeeds and returns the cwd') but concluded that empty would 'reach the -z test'; it does not. The third change (abs_dir rejecting empty) is what actually delivers the brief's stated intent, and it keeps the reviewed-clean condition block untouched, which the alternative (adding a raw `-z "$SNAP_TOP"` to the condition) would not have. This is the same vacuous-green class the unit has now hit four times, so it was not left for round 5.

cases: (i) toplevel is a path that does not exist
arm.why_both: They fail in OPPOSITE directions — (i) used to abort into a false BLOCK, (ii) would become a false PASS — and one fix must handle both.
